gates.reason: Pure in-memory recommendation calculation with no auth, filesystem, network/LLM egress, command execution, HTML sink, or secret handling.
Verified defects misprice mixed-model turns and count any model-ID change as a downgrade, corrupting savings and downgradable-percentage claims.
Verified quadratic fallback rescans every token entry for every turn whenever timestamps or slices are non-monotonic.
Inspected untrusted upload parsing; values are type-checked and only copied into inert records, with no execution, write, egress, or web sink.
The parser reproducibly derives session ID, per-mode rows, and ordered mode transitions directly from filename, permissionMode, and timestamp fields.
Upload ingestion is a single linear pass with no repeated parsing or nested scan.
Dangerous command samples remain inert strings, and regression assertions cover destructive-shell detection, quoting, heredocs, redirects, and force-push variants without executing them.
Assertions explicitly verify permission transitions, dangerous-command evidence and certainty, safety-score arithmetic, and prompt-prone-tool aggregation.
Test-only code is not an ingest or request hot path and ships no runtime surface.

findings.title: Mixed-model turns are repriced as though every entry used the first model
findings.what: pickModelForEntry selects one model for the entire turn, then entryCostAt prices every TokenEntry using that model's tier. If a turn contains entries from different models, actualCostUsd is not the cost actually incurred; estimated savings and all roll-ups derived from it are therefore unreproducible from the entries' model fields.
findings.fix: Compute actualCost by resolving pricing independently for each entry's model, with an explicit documented fallback only for entries lacking a usable model. Continue pricing recommendedCost against the single recommendation target.
findings.acceptance: Add a mixed-model turn containing token entries with two deliberately different pricing tiers and assert actualCostUsd equals the sum of each entry priced by its own model; assert savings and session/summary totals use that corrected amount.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 367-371 choose the first non-synthetic model and lines 495-505 pass one pricing object to every entry; no per-entry pricing occurs in either branch.

findings.title: The downgradable metric counts upgrades and model aliases as downgrades
findings.what: downgradable is incremented whenever currentModel and recommendedModel are unequal. This includes an unknown current model being mapped to Opus and distinct IDs within the same model family, neither of which establishes a cheaper downgrade. The resulting downgradableTurns and downgradablePct claims can be false even when savings is clamped to zero.
findings.fix: Increment downgradable only when the recommendation has a strictly lower resolved price/capability tier than the observed current model; treat unknown pricing and equivalent-family aliases as not proven downgradable.
findings.acceptance: Add cases for unknown-to-Opus, old-Sonnet-ID-to-current-Sonnet-ID, a true Opus-to-Sonnet downgrade, and an unchanged model; only the proven cheaper transition may increase downgradableTurns or downgradablePct.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed the metric uses raw string inequality at line 490, while the displayed session and global percentages directly aggregate that counter without a price or family comparison.

findings.title: Non-monotonic input triggers turns-by-tokens rescanning
findings.what: When either token timestamps or turn slices are non-monotonic, each turn calls collectTokenEntriesForWindowUnsorted, which scans the complete token array. A session with T turns and N token entries therefore degrades from approximately O(T+N) to O(T×N), with a fresh result array allocated for each turn.
findings.fix: Normalize token entries once into timestamp order and use a cursor or binary-search window boundaries; preserve original-order semantics separately only where required for malformed equal/invalid timestamps.
findings.acceptance: A regression benchmark or operation-count test using reversed token timestamps and many turns must show token-entry examinations grow near-linearly (or O((T+N) log N)), not T×N, while producing the same turn attribution.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the fallback loop at lines 360-363 traverses all timed entries and is invoked inside the per-slice loop at lines 428 and 445-449.
